§28.25 Asymptotic Expansions for Large ℜ⁡z

ⓘ

For fixed h(≠0) and fixed ν,

28.25.1 Mν(3,4)⁡(z,h)∼e±i⁢(2⁢h⁢cosh⁡z−(12⁢ν+14)⁢π)(π⁢h⁢(cosh⁡z+1))12⁢∑m=0∞Dm±(∓4⁢i⁢h⁢(cosh⁡z+1))m,
ⓘ
Symbols:
∼: Poincaré asymptotic expansion, π: the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter, e: base of natural logarithm, cosh⁡z: hyperbolic cosine function, i: imaginary unit, Mν(j)⁡(z,h): modified Mathieu function, m: integer, h: parameter, z: complex variable, ν: complex parameter and Dm±: coefficients
A&S Ref:
20.9.1 (for 3 and for integer ν) 20.9.3 (for 4 and for integer ν)

The upper signs correspond to Mν(3)⁡(z,h) and the lower signs to Mν(4)⁡(z,h). The expansion (28.25.1) is valid for Mν(3)⁡(z,h) when

28.25.4 ℜ⁡z→+∞,
−π+δ≤ph⁡h+ℑ⁡z≤2⁢π−δ,
ⓘ
Symbols:
π: the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter, ℑ⁡: imaginary part, ph: phase, ℜ⁡: real part, h: parameter, z: complex variable and δ: arbitrary small positive constant
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/28.25.E4
Encodings:
TeX, pMML, png
See also:
Annotations for §28.25 and Ch.28

and for Mν(4)⁡(z,h) when

28.25.5 ℜ⁡z→+∞,
−2⁢π+δ≤ph⁡h+ℑ⁡z≤π−δ,
ⓘ
Symbols:
π: the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter, ℑ⁡: imaginary part, ph: phase, ℜ⁡: real part, h: parameter, z: complex variable and δ: arbitrary small positive constant
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/28.25.E5
Encodings:
TeX, pMML, png
See also:
Annotations for §28.25 and Ch.28

where δ again denotes an arbitrary small positive constant.

For proofs and generalizations see Meixner and Schäfke (1954, §2.63).
